name: Ruwanwelisaya
description: One of the world's tallest ancient monuments and a masterpiece of Sinhalese engineering.
history: Commissioned by the hero-king Dutugemunu to enshrine sacred relics, Ruwanwelisaya (The Great Stupa) was his magnum opus. The Mahavamsa records that the king fell ill and passed away just before its completion; his brother Saddha Tissa covered the unfinished dome with white cloth to show the dying king what it would look like.
construction: Originally standing at 103 meters (338 ft) with a circumference of 290 meters, it was one of the tallest structures in the ancient world. The foundation was stabilized using crushed stone and elephants equipped with leather boots to stomp the ground flat.
architecture: The stupa follows the 'Bubulakara' (bubble-shaped) design. It features a 'vahalkada' (frontispiece) at each of the four cardinal points, adorned with elephant carvings. The 'Hatharas Kotuwa' (square enclosure) and 'Devatha Kotuwa' (deity enclosure) sit atop the dome.
significance: It is revered as the 'Mahathupa' (Great Stupa) and is one of the Solosmasthana (16 sacred places) and Atamasthana (8 sacred places) in Anuradhapura. It is believed to house the largest collection of Buddha's relics in the world.
currentStatus: A major pilgrimage site for Buddhists globally, the stupa was renovated in the early 20th century and stands today at 103 meters.

name: Jetavanaramaya
description: Once the tallest stupa in the ancient world, standing at 122 meters.
history: Built by King Mahasena following the destruction of the Mahavihara monastery, it was gifted to the Sagaliya sect. The construction marked a period of theological conflict between Theravada and Mahayana traditions in ancient Sri Lanka.
construction: Constructed using approximately 93 million baked bricks, it was the third tallest structure in the world upon completion, surpassed only by the Great Pyramids of Giza. Its original height was estimated at 122 meters (400 ft).
architecture: The stupa represents a massive engineering feat with a deep foundation resting on bedrock. It follows the traditional stupa architectural elements but on a colossal scale.
significance: It is the largest stupa in the world by volume and a testament to the advanced engineering capabilities of the Anuradhapura Kingdom.
currentStatus: Extensive conservation work by the Central Cultural Fund has stabilized the structure. It currently stands around 71 meters tall.

name: Abhayagiri Dagoba
description: Major Buddhist monastery complex and one of the most important monasteries in ancient Sri Lanka.

name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
description: Ancient rock fortress and palace with famous frescoes, UNESCO World Heritage Site.
history: According to the Mahavamsa, King Kashyapa I (477–495 CE) selected this site as his new capital after usurping the throne from his father. He built his palace on the top of this massive rock column and decorated its sides with colourful frescoes. On a small plateau about halfway up the side of this rock, he built a gateway in the form of an enormous lion. The name of this place is derived from this structure — Sīhāgiri, the Lion Rock. The capital and the royal palace were abandoned after the king's death in battle, and it was used as a Buddhist monastery until the 14th century.
construction: The fortress complex includes remnants of a ruined palace, surrounded by an extensive network of fortifications, vast gardens, ponds, canals, alleys, and fountains. The summit of the rock is 1.6 hectares in area, housing the royal citadel.
architecture: Sigiriya is famous for its frescoes, which depict damsels or 'apsaras' in a style similar to the Ajanta Caves. The 'Mirror Wall', originally so well polished that the king could see his reflection in it, is now covered with verses scribbled by visitors dating back to the 8th century. The Water Gardens showcase advanced hydraulic engineering, utilizing a complex system of underground conduits and gravity-fed fountains, some of which are still functional today.
significance: Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982, Sigiriya is one of the best-preserved examples of ancient urban planning. It is often referred to by locals as the Eighth Wonder of the World due to its engineering and artistic marvels.
currentStatus: It is a major tourist destination and a protected archaeological site managed by the Central Cultural Fund of Sri Lanka.

name: Sri Maha Bodhi
description: Sacred fig tree grown from a cutting of the original Bodhi tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment.

name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
description: Temple housing the relic of the tooth of Buddha, UNESCO World Heritage Site.
history: The Sacred Tooth Relic (Dalada) was brought to Sri Lanka in the 4th century CE. It became the palladium of kingship—whoever possessed it had the divine right to rule. The current two-story shrine was built by King Sri Veera Parakrama Narendrasinghe (1707-1739), with later additions by the last king, Sri Vikrama Rajasinha (the Octagon).
construction: The temple complex is located within the royal palace grounds. It is built on a granite base with walls of limestone and timber upper floors.
architecture: The architecture features typical Kandyan elements: a high-pitched roof, white walls with cloud drift walls (Walakulu Bemma), and the famous Octagon (Paththirippuwa). The interior is richly decorated with ivory, lacquer work, and intricate wood carvings.
significance: It is the most sacred Buddhist site in Sri Lanka and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The annual Esala Perahera procession centers around the relic.
currentStatus: It remains a center of daily worship and a major tourist attraction. The relic is kept in seven nesting gold caskets.

name: Polonnaruwa Vatadage
description: Circular relic house with finest stone carvings and moonstone entrances.
history: Built during the Polonnaruwa period to house the Tooth Relic. While some attribute it to Parakramabahu I, others suggest Nissanka Malla embellished it.
construction: A circular structure with two concentric stone terraces.
architecture: Famous for its moonstones (sandakada pahana) and guardstones (muragala) which are considered the finest examples of Polonnaruwa art. Four seated Buddha statues face the four cardinal directions.
significance: It is the best-preserved example of a 'Vatadage' (circular relic house) in Sri Lanka.
currentStatus: A well-preserved archaeological ruin in the Dalada Maluwa (Quadrangle) of Polonnaruwa.

name: Gal Vihara
description: Group of four magnificent rock relief Buddha statues carved from a single granite rock wall.
history: Part of the Uttararama (Northern Monastery) commissioned by King Parakramabahu I. The chronicle Chulavamsa records the creation of these images.
construction: The four statues are carved into a single large granite rock face.
architecture: The complex includes a seated Buddha in deep meditation, a smaller seated Buddha inside a cave, a standing figure with crossed arms (often debated to be Ananda or the Buddha), and a massive reclining Buddha (14 meters long) depicting Parinirvana.
significance: Considered the masterpiece of Sinhalese rock carving. The fluid drapery and serene expressions demonstrate the peak of Polonnaruwa era artistry.
currentStatus: A protected archaeological site and an active place of worship.

name: Dambulla Cave Temple
description: Largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka with over 150 Buddha statues.
history: King Valagamba took refuge in these caves for 14 years when he was exiled by South Indian invaders. Upon reclaiming his throne, he converted the caves into magnificent temples in gratitude.
construction: The complex consists of five main caves under a vast overhanging rock, rising 160 meters over the surrounding plains.
architecture: The cave ceilings are painted with intricate patterns and religious scenes covering 2,100 square meters. The complex houses 153 Buddha statues, 3 statues of Sri Lankan kings, and 4 statues of gods and goddesses.
significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site (1991), it is the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in the country.
currentStatus: A major pilgrimage site and tourist attraction.

name: Lovamahapaya (Brazen Palace)
description: Nine-storey monastic building said to have had a bronze roof with 1,600 granite columns.

name: Thuparamaya
description: First Buddhist stupa built in Sri Lanka, enshrining the right collarbone of Buddha.

name: Isurumuniya Temple
description: Rock temple famous for the Isurumuniya Lovers sculpture and ancient carvings.

name: Mihintale
description: Sacred mountain where Buddhism was introduced to Sri Lanka by Mahinda.

name: Lankatilaka Temple
description: Ancient Buddhist temple built on a rock with impressive architecture.

name: Embekka Devalaya
description: Hindu temple famous for intricate wood carvings depicting dancers, musicians, and mythical creatures.

name: Gadaladeniya Temple
description: Buddhist temple with South Indian architectural influences built on a rocky outcrop.

name: Yapahuwa Rock Fortress
description: Rock fortress with ornate staircase that once housed the Sacred Tooth Relic.

name: Parakrama Samudra
description: Massive ancient irrigation reservoir demonstrating advanced hydraulic engineering.

name: Royal Palace of Polonnaruwa
description: Seven-storey royal palace complex with impressive architectural remains.

name: Rankot Vehera
description: Fourth largest stupa in Sri Lanka and largest in Polonnaruwa.

name: Kiri Vehera
description: Well-preserved white stupa built by the queen, still retaining its original lime plaster.

name: Medirigiriya Vatadage
description: Ancient circular relic house with concentric stone columns and Buddha statues.

name: Avukana Buddha Statue
description: Standing Buddha statue carved from a single granite rock, 40 feet tall.

name: Ritigala Monastery
description: Ancient forest monastery complex with unique architectural features.

name: Buduruwagala
description: Seven large rock-carved Buddha statues, the tallest being 51 feet.

name: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil
description: One of the most significant Hindu temples in Sri Lanka, dedicated to Lord Murugan. The original temple was founded in the 10th century but the current structure dates back to the 15th century, built by Sapumal Kumaraya (who later became King Bhuvanaikabahu VI of Kotte) during his administration of the Jaffna Kingdom.

name: Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara
description: An ancient Buddhist temple believed to have been hallowed during the third and final visit of the Lord Buddha to Sri Lanka. It was the capital of the regional King Kelanitissa. The temple is famous for its image house paintings and the annual Duruthu Perahera.

name: Lankarama
description: A stupa built by King Valagamba in an ancient place named Galhebakada. It is one of the eight sacred places (Atamasthana) in Anuradhapura. The stupa was originally surrounded by a vatadage (stupa house), of which only stone pillars remain.

name: Mirisawetiya Vihara
description: The first stupa built by King Dutugemunu after his victory over King Elara. Legend says the king went to bathe in the Tissa Wewa leaving his sceptre (kunta) with a Buddha relic planted in the ground. When he returned, it could not be moved, so he built the stupa over it.

name: Tōdai-ji Temple & Great Buddha
description: Historic Buddhist temple complex in Nara housing the Daibutsu (Great Bronze Buddha), one of the largest wooden buildings in the world.

name: Himeji Castle (White Heron Castle)
description: Japan's most pristine surviving feudal castle, featuring an intricate defensive maze of gates, walls, and brilliant white plaster architecture.

name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
description: Iconic Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto covered in pure gold leaf, reflecting seamlessly across the Kyoko-chi mirror pond.

name: Great Pyramids of Giza & Great Sphinx
description: The monumental funerary complex on the Giza Plateau housing the Great Pyramid of Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure, and the monolithic limestone Sphinx.

name: Karnak Temple Complex
description: Vast open-air temple complex dedicated to the Theban triad of Amun, Mut, and Khonsu, featuring the colossal Great Hypostyle Hall.

name: Abu Simbel Temples
description: Twin massive rock-cut temples carved into a mountainside by Ramses II in Nubia, featuring four colossal 20-meter seated statues of the pharaoh.

name: The Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre)
description: The largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, capable of seating 50,000 spectators for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.

name: The Pantheon
description: Masterpiece of Roman engineering commissioned by Marcus Agrippa and rebuilt by Hadrian, retaining the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.

name: Ruins of Pompeii
description: Remarkably preserved Roman city buried under volcanic ash from Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE, providing vivid insight into daily imperial life.

name: Great Stupa at Sanchi
description: One of the oldest stone structures in India commissioned by Emperor Ashoka, featuring intricate torana gateways illustrating Buddhist jatakas.

name: Taj Mahal
description: Ivory-white marble mausoleum on the Yamuna river in Agra commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

name: Parthenon on the Acropolis
description: Former temple on the Athenian Acropolis dedicated to the goddess Athena, regarded as the enduring zenith of Classical Greek Doric architecture.

name: Persepolis (Takht-e Jamshid)
description: Grand ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire built by Darius I and Xerxes, showcasing the Gate of All Nations and Apadana Palace reliefs.

name: Terracotta Army of Qin Shi Huang
description: Colossal underground army of over 8,000 life-sized terracotta soldiers, chariots, and horses buried to protect China's first emperor in the afterlife.

name: The Great Wall of China
description: Vast series of stone and rammed-earth fortifications stretching thousands of kilometers across northern China, featuring watchtowers and garrisons.

name: The Forbidden City
description: Imperial palace complex in the heart of Beijing housing 24 emperors across the Ming and Qing dynasties with 980 surviving wooden palace buildings.

name: Great Ziggurat of Ur
description: Massive stepped mud-brick pyramid temple dedicated to the moon god Nanna, built during the Neo-Sumerian revival.

name: Ishtar Gate & Ruins of Babylon
description: The eighth inner gate of Babylon adorned with vibrant blue glazed bricks and bas-relief dragons (Mušḫuššu) and young bulls.

name: Pyramids of Teotihuacan
description: Ancient holy city featuring the monumental Pyramid of the Sun, Pyramid of the Moon, and the Avenue of the Dead.

name: Chichen Itza (El Castillo)
description: Famous Maya-Toltec ceremonial city centered around the Temple of Kukulcan step pyramid, engineered with equinox shadow serpents.

name: Machu Picchu (Lost City of the Incas)
description: 15th-century Inca citadel perched on a mountain ridge above the Sacred Valley, showcasing polished dry-stone ashlar masonry.

name: Sacsayhuamán Fortress
description: Inca fortress on the northern outskirts of Cusco with colossal zig-zag limestone walls fitted so tightly that not even a sheet of paper can pass between them.

name: Stonehenge Megalithic Monument
description: Prehistoric stone circle monument on Salisbury Plain, aligned with the sunrise on the summer solstice and sunset on the winter solstice.

name: Tower of London (Her Majesty's Royal Palace and Fortress)
description: Historic castle founded towards the end of 1066 as part of the Norman Conquest of England, housing the Crown Jewels.

name: Palace of Versailles
description: Principal royal residence of France under Louis XIV, featuring the legendary Hall of Mirrors, Grand Canal, and Baroque garden architecture.

name: Rock-Hewn Churches of Lalibela
description: Eleven medieval monolithic cave churches carved directly downward out of volcanic rock, including the cruciform Church of Saint George (Biete Ghiorgis).

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
description: The largest sun-baked earth (adobe) building in the world, considered by many architects to be the crowning achievement of the Sudano-Sahelian style.
